candidates.name: Castell de la Santa Bàrbara
candidates.alt: Castillo de Santa Bárbara / Castle of Santa Barbara
candidates.hours: Oct-Mar daily 10:00-20:00, Apr-Jun daily 10:00-22:00, Jul Aug daily 10:00-24:00, Sep daily 10:00-22:00
candidates.content: On top of Mount Benacantil at a height of 166 metres, there is one of the largest medieval fortresses in Spain, built in the ninth century by Muslims. An amazing view of town and harbour. If you feel fit, the walk from Plaza

candidates.name: Basílica de Santa Maria
candidates.content: Begun during the 14th century on top of the remains of an old Moorish mosque, construction was completed in the 16th century, and incorporates Gothic and Baroque stylistic elements in its structure. The main entrance to the church

candidates.name: Museu Arqueològic Provincial d'Alacant
candidates.alt: MARQ / Museo Arqueológico de Alicante / Archaeological Museum of Alicante
candidates.content: Founded in 1932, it was originally located in the ground floor of the Diputación Palace, and in 2000 it moved to its current location, the former Provincial Hospital building. The museum has an avant-garde design and uses modern a

candidates.name: Museu de Belles Arts Gravina
candidates.hours: 1 Sep - 30 Jun: Tue-Sat 10:00-20:00, Sun and holidays 10:00-14:00; 1 Jul - 31 Aug: Tue-Sat 11:00-21:00, Sun and holidays 11:00-15:00
candidates.content: This local fine arts museum, housed in an 18th-century palace, has some excellent artworks by Spanish artists, displayed over 3 floors. Take time to watch the video presentation Black and White about historic Alicante.

candidates.name: Museu d'Art Contemporani d'Alacant
candidates.content: On display there are a few works by world-famous artists of the 20th century: Pablo Picasso, Georges Braque, Julio González, Juan Gris, Joan Miró; as well as art collections by two local artists Eusebio Sempere and Juana Francés.

candidates.name: Coves del Canelobre
candidates.hours: 1 Sep - 30 Jun: Tue-Fri 10:30-16:50, Sat Sun and holidays 10:30-17:50; 1 Jul - 31 Aug: daily 10:30-19:30; Easter Sun 10:30-19:30; closed Mon after Easter, 25 Dec and 1 Jan
candidates.content: A large cave network with impressive stalacites and stalagmites. The inner aspect of the main cave, with one of the highest vaults of Spain, is very similar to the one of a cathedral. Visitors are able to admire the diverse and ca

candidates.name: Lucentum Archaeological Site
candidates.content: This site, which covers over 7 acres, is the location of the original Roman city which later became Alicante. Although excavation is ongoing, it is open to visitors. Notable features are remains of the defensive walls, Roman baths

candidates.name: Museu de la Ciutat d'Alacant
candidates.alt: MUSA / Museo de la Ciudad / Museum of the City of Alicante
candidates.content: Showcases archaeological finds from the city and the region.

candidates.name: Castell de Sant Ferran
candidates.alt: Castillo de San Fernando / Castle of San Fernando
candidates.content: Built at the beginning of the 19th century, the fortress is now the centrepiece of a city park.

candidates.name: Museu de la Universitat d’Alacant
candidates.alt: Museo de la Universidad de Alicante / MUA
candidates.content: Opened in 1999, this ultra-modern museum is devoted to contemporary art and hosts special exhibits as well as concerts and other events.There are exhibits in three locations next to each other.

candidates.name: Museu d’Aigües d’Alacant
candidates.alt: Museo de Aguas de Alicante / Alicante Water Museum
candidates.content: The museum is adjacent to the Pozos de Garrigós (Garrigós Wells), a collection of wells dating from the Moorish period to the 16th century, and in use until 1898. Exhibits in the three-floor modern museum illustrate the history of

candidates.name: Teatre Principal
candidates.content: Alicante's main theatre was built in the mid-19th century, and partially destroyed and rebuilt during the Spanish Civil War. Today it is the city's main venue for not only plays but also musicals, dance, and musical performances.

candidates.name: Auditori de la Diputació d'Alacant
candidates.alt: Auditorio de la Diputación de Alicante
candidates.content: A venue for classical music performances, by both Spanish and international musicians. The building was designed by Alicante-born architect Juan Antonio García Solera.

candidates.name: Fogueres de Sant Joan
candidates.alt: Hogueras de San Juan / Bonfires of Saint John
candidates.content: The most important festival in the city, with preparations beginning a week beforehand. Throughout Alicante, enormous monuments (up to and above 3 stories tall) are constructed and burned at the end of the festival during the nigh

candidates.name: Moros i Cristians
candidates.alt: Moros y Cristianos / Moors and Christians
candidates.content: One of the many Moorish and Christian festivals in the province, here the tradition began in the 20th century. Different neighbourhoods in the city celebrate at different times of year. In the Villafranqueza it is celebrated in Ma

candidates.name: Carnaval
candidates.hours: February to March, just before Lent
candidates.content: Features parades of people in disguises and open air concerts (yes, weather allows it!).

candidates.name: Setmana Santa
candidates.content: Has parades of religious brotherhoods with their images of Jesus Christ and Holy Mary.

candidates.name: Romiatge de Santa Faç
candidates.alt: Romería de Santa Faz / Pilgrimage of Santa Faz
candidates.content: A massive pilgrimage/walk to the (Spanish: Monasterio de la Santa Faz), where a relic with and image of Jesus is on display.

candidates.name: Epifanía
candidates.content: As in the rest of Spain, in the Epiphany (January the 6th) there is a parade in remembrance of the Three Wise Men that adored Child Jesus, where every child participates (it is the equivalent to Santa Claus in the Spanish culture)

candidates.name: Gay Pride
candidates.content: It is usually held in July. During this week Alicante fills up with artistic and cultural activities. The last day a manifesto is read in Plaza Mayor del Ayuntamiento where afterwards music is played and people drink and dance.

candidates.name: Kinépolis
candidates.content: A modern cineplex which shows the latest blockbusters, with both dubbed and original language versions (VOS: versión original subtitulada).

candidates.name: Yelmo Cines
candidates.content: Another cineplex which shows current films in both dubbed and original language versions.

candidates.name: Sylvarum Cocktail Bar
candidates.content: Botanically inspired signature cocktails (the name is Latin for "of the forests"), served in a space of stone, wood and plants with a back lounge of leather sofas. Besides the menu, the bartenders will make a cocktail to order bas

candidates.name: Sala Stereo
candidates.content: Concert venue for around 280 people, with indie, rock and electronic music. On Friday and Saturday nights, DJ sessions start at 03:30 and run until morning.

candidates.name: The Whisper
candidates.content: Cocktail bar inspired by the Prohibition era, serving classics and house creations.

candidates.name: La Terraza de Amérigo
candidates.content: Signature cocktails and tapas with views of Santa Bárbara Castle.

candidates.name: La Milagrosa Rooftop
candidates.content: Rooftop of the B&B La Milagrosa, at the foot of the castle next to the Basilica of Santa María. Best at sunset.

candidates.name: Highbar
candidates.content: On the roof of the Odyssey Rooms hotel, with a pool that can be booked.

candidates.name: Mira Miralta
candidates.content: Rooftop bar of the Eurostars Pórtico hotel, next to the Town Hall square. Open to non-guests.

candidates.name: Cuppola
candidates.content: Rooftop of the DormirDCine hotel in the old town, serving film-inspired cocktails.

candidates.name: Convistas
candidates.content: Restaurant and bar with panoramic views over the city, the marina and the sea.

candidates.name: El Muelle Live
candidates.content: Open-air venue in the port. On Saturdays from 11:00, free entry to live music, DJs and street-food stalls; big ticketed concerts in summer.

candidates.name: Sausalito
candidates.content: Cocktail lounge and club in the port.

candidates.name: Sala Clan Cabaret
candidates.content: Live shows and dancing until the early hours.

candidates.name: Sala The One
candidates.content: Large venue for around 1,000 people, hosting rock, punk and post-punk concerts and club nights. Popular with students.

candidates.name: Nou Manolin
candidates.content: A very popular restaurant which focuses on regional specialties. On the ground floor is a great tapas bar, while formal dining is on the upper floors. Also has a great wine cellar.

candidates.name: Monastrell
candidates.content: Michelin-starred chef María José San Román focuses on contemporary and avant-garde cuisine, relying on local products. The minimalist dining area is decorated with wood, aluminum, and granite. Reservations can be made online.

candidates.name: El Nou Cisne
candidates.content: Serves tapas and raciones.

candidates.name: Piripi
candidates.content: A popular restaurant best known for its tapas and rice dishes.

candidates.name: La Taberna del Gourmet
candidates.price: Tapas €7-19, tapas tasting menu €27.50, standard tasting menu €55 (May 2016)
candidates.content: A well-known tapas bar and delicatessen, with fine wines.

candidates.name: Restaurante Capri
candidates.content: A great experience in tapas. Excellent food, good service and cleanliness.

candidates.name: Tapeo Manila Bar de tapas restaurante
candidates.content: Nice and cozy place. Excellent food and drink. Good place to stop and have a snack.

candidates.name: Dársena
candidates.content: A long-established and respected restaurant, known especially for paella and other rice dishes, and for seafood. This place is very busy and reservations are recommended.

candidates.name: Restaurante La Matanza Castellana
candidates.content: Good dishes and high quality meat. Menu of the day more than correct. The slaughter rice is very rich and the sirloin is grilled very well. Kind waiters.

candidates.name: 100 Montaditos
candidates.content: Great place for a quick meal, as the service is fast. There is a vegetarian menu. Large portions. Cheese balls are just amazing. The quality is good for this type of establishment. There are tables on the second floor.

candidates.name: Unik Asiatico Restaurante
candidates.content: Always a delight. Popular Chinese restaurant. Pretty authentic taste. The food is always fresh and delicious. The fried sushi and the Taiwanese rice with pineapple are just brilliant. Excellent service and very welcoming.

candidates.name: La Tasca Del Barrio
candidates.content: Very good food and attention. Particularly recommended is the la tasca salad, the jamon is melt in the mouth delicious. You need to reserve if you'd like to sit inside. Nice staff.

candidates.name: Mercat Central
candidates.content: The two levels sell all the fresh meat, seafood, cheeses, fruit and vegetables anyone could need. If you exit the market through the back, you'll find the flower sellers in a small outdoor square.

candidates.name: Mercat Babel
candidates.content: A standard food market selling local produce and fish. On Th and Sa mornings there is also an outdoor market along the adjacent streets where you can pick up various other household goods, clothings, etc.

candidates.name: Mercat Benalúa
candidates.content: A standard food market, with a nearby outdoor street market on Thursday and Saturday mornings.

candidates.name: Mercat Carolinas
candidates.content: A standard food market, with a nearby outdoor street market on Thursday and Saturday mornings.

candidates.name: Passeig Esplanada d'Espanya market
candidates.hours: Mon Wed-Fri 11:30-14:30 17:00-20:30, Sat Sun and holidays 11:00-22:30
candidates.content: Market stalls along the promenade selling beads, clothes, flags etc.
